title: Sleepy cod

identification.basis: The dictionary's kurrubal is 'fresh water cod', and the sleepy cod is the only freshwater fish called a cod on this coast; the identification is a reasonable guess, not a record. The sleepy cod is recorded within 30 km of Karma Waters.

summary: **[kurrubal](word:kurrubal)** is 'fresh water cod', and the freshwater cod of these rivers is the sleepy cod, *Oxyeleotris lineolata*, a thick, mottled, big-headed fish that lies on the bottom among snags and roots by day and hunts by night, and that is 'one of the most favoured freshwater fish in Australia for eating, having white, flaky flesh, low fat content, and a mild flavour' [ref:hershberger1982] [ref:wiki-sleepy-cod]. It is not a cod at all but a gudgeon, in the family Butidae, 'thus is unrelated to the true cods' [ref:wiki-sleepy-cod]. It reaches 51 cm and 3 kg, though most are under 20 cm; it lives 'in quiet or slow-flowing water among vegetation, around log debris or beneath undercut banks'; it can breathe air; and from October to February the male guards a sheet of up to 70,000 eggs 'which look like shiny velvet' stuck to the roof of a hollow log or the underside of a ledge until they hatch [ref:wiki-sleepy-cod] [ref:fishbase-sleepy] [ref:nfa-sleepy].

infobox.label: Size
infobox.value: To 51 cm and 3 kg; most under 20 cm

infobox.label: Look
infobox.value: Dark brown back, paler sides with fuzzy dark lines along the scale rows; big head and mouth; rounded tail; young with a cream stripe along the back

infobox.label: Where
infobox.value: Quiet, slow water among weed, snags, log debris and undercut banks; Fitzroy River north through Cape York, the Gulf and west to the Ord

infobox.label: Food
infobox.value: Fish, insects, prawns and crustaceans; sits by day, takes live food at night

infobox.label: Breeding
infobox.value: October–February; a sheet of up to 70,000 adhesive eggs on the roof of a log or the underside of a ledge, guarded and fanned by the male, hatching in 5–7 days

infobox.label: Rules
infobox.value: Not listed in the Queensland freshwater size and possession table

sections.heading: Names
sections.body: **[kurrubal](word:kurrubal)** 'fresh water cod' [ref:hershberger1982]. Nothing else in the dictionary fits the sleepy cod so well, and nothing says outright that this is the fish; the gloss is a colonist's name applied to a Kuku Yalanji word, and the identification is this page's. Other river fish words: **[kuyu](word:kuyu)** 'fish'; **[kurruba](word:kurruba)** 'species of freshwater fish'; **[bayil](word:bayil)** 'jungle perch'; **[dijarr](word:dijarr)** a perch 'like the jungle perch, but not around here. Found at Rossville and Shipton's Flats'; **[julaji](word:julaji)** and **[kanyaji](word:kanyaji)** the [catfish](entry:catfish) [ref:hershberger1982]. In English the fish is the sleepy cod, 'sleepy' for the way it lies, and 'cod' for its shape and its eating, though it is a gudgeon [ref:wiki-sleepy-cod].

sections.heading: The fish
sections.body:
'The sleepy cod can reach a length of 51 cm, though most do not exceed 20 cm. Fish up to 3 kg have been caught by anglers. They are dark brown along the back and paler on the sides, with fuzzy dark lines running along scale rows. Juveniles have a white or cream patch running along the back and top of the head, with brown sides and a white belly' [ref:wiki-sleepy-cod]. FishBase: maximum 45 cm standard length, common 20 cm; 'facultative air-breathing in the genus' [ref:fishbase-sleepy].

'Most often found in slow flowing well vegetated areas with abundant in-stream cover, snags and submerged logs'; 'widespread from the Fitzroy River in Queensland north throughout Cape York, the Gulf of Carpentaria and west to the Ord River system' [ref:nfa-sleepy]. 'A sluggish bottom dwelling carnivore, feeds on other fish, insects and crustaceans'; 'generally quiet during the day it will take live food such as other fish, shrimps etc at night' [ref:nfa-sleepy].

**Breeding.** 'Spawning occurs between October and February. Female lays a roundish egg sheet, of up to 70,000 adhesive eggs. This is frequently on the underside of an overhanging rock ledge, under roots or on the roof of a hollow submerged log, usually in a shady location. The straw coloured eggs, which look like shiny velvet, are guarded and aerated by the male until after the eggs hatch in 5 to 7 days' [ref:nfa-sleepy] [ref:wiki-sleepy-cod].

'A popular angling species, although it offers little in the way of sport' [ref:nfa-sleepy]. 'They are one of the most favoured freshwater fish in Australia for eating' [ref:wiki-sleepy-cod]. FishBase rates it 'moderate vulnerability' [ref:fishbase-sleepy].

sections.heading: Sleepy cod, catfish, barramundi
sections.body:
- **Sleepy cod**: mottled brown, big flat head, rounded tail, no whiskers, lying on the bottom [ref:wiki-sleepy-cod].
- **[Catfish](entry:catfish)**: whiskers, a pointed eel-like tail, and venomous fin spines [ref:hershberger1982].
- **[Barramundi](entry:barramundi)**: silver, humped, broom-tailed, a mid-water hunter [ref:wiki-saratoga].
- **[Mouth almighty](entry:mouth-almighty)**: small, barred, with two back fins and a bar through the eye, in the weed at the edge [ref:wiki-mouth-almighty].
- **Purple-spotted gudgeon and the small gudgeons**: the same family, a hand long at most [ref:fishbase-sleepy].

sections.heading: Signs
sections.body:
- **A shape on the bottom beside a log** that does not move when you look at it; the fish lies still by day [ref:nfa-sleepy].
- **A velvet sheet of straw-coloured eggs** on the roof of a hollow log or under a ledge in the shade, with a male beside it, from October [ref:nfa-sleepy].
- **Prawn shells** in the shallows at dawn: the night's hunting [ref:jardine2012].
- **A fish gulping at the surface** of a hot, still pool in the late dry is using its air-breathing [ref:fishbase-sleepy] [ref:waterhole-temps].

sections.heading: Where it lives
sections.body: 'Quiet or slow-flowing water among vegetation, around log debris or beneath undercut banks' in 'rivers, creeks and billabongs' [ref:fishbase-sleepy]. The [waterhole](entry:waterhole) page describes the cover, and the hot, low-oxygen water of the late dry that its air-breathing helps it through [ref:waterhole-temps] [ref:fergusson-refuge].

sections.heading: The night shift on the bottom
sections.body: The sleepy cod takes the bottom of the pool at night: prawns, [cherabin](entry:cherabin), insects, small fish, among the snags, while the [catfish](entry:catfish) work the open bottom and the [eels](entry:eels) the edges, and the [mouth almighty](entry:mouth-almighty) ambushes in the weed [ref:nfa-sleepy] [ref:jardine2012]. By day it lies up, and that is when the [freshwater crocodile](entry:freshwater-crocodile), the darter and the cormorant find it [ref:tucker1996] [ref:wiki-darter]. Its eggs on the roof of a log are a fortnight's work for the male and food for everything that finds them; the [waterhole](entry:waterhole) page has the pool's whole cast.

sections.heading: Seasons
sections.body: Spawning October to February, as the water warms past 25 °C and the first storms come; males on the nests then [ref:nfa-sleepy] [ref:waterhole-temps]. Through the dry it is in the deep cover of the pools, most active on warm nights; in the late dry, when the pools shrink and go hot and low in oxygen, the air-breathing gudgeons are among the last fish still comfortable [ref:fishbase-sleepy] [ref:fergusson-refuge]. See [the year on country](entry:seasons).

sections.heading: Uses
sections.body:
- The best eating fish in the river: white, flaky, mild, low in fat [ref:wiki-sleepy-cod].
- Easy to keep alive and carry: 'tolerates capture, handling and transport well' [ref:nfa-sleepy].
- Taken by spear from the bank by day where it lies, by line at night, and in traps and fences [ref:anderson1996] [ref:roth1901].

sections.heading: Taking a sleepy cod
sections.body:
The ways of taking river fish are on their own pages: [spears](entry:spear-and-woomera), [nets](entry:nets), [traps and fences](entry:fish-traps), [hooks and lines](entry:hooks-and-lines) and [fish poisons](entry:fish-poisoning). At Bloomfield, night fishing was 'done on the tidal estuaries from a canoe at night. One person sat at the front of the boat holding aloft a burning paperbark torch. As the fish were attracted to the light, another person would spear them' [ref:anderson1996].

1. **By day, by spear**: walk the bank of a clear pool and look beside the logs and under the overhangs for the mottled shape lying still; the many-pronged *yirrmba* is the spear for a fish that does not move [ref:nfa-sleepy] [ref:hershberger1982].
2. **By night, by line**: a live prawn or a piece of fish on a [hook](entry:hooks-and-lines) dropped beside a snag; it 'will take live food such as other fish, shrimps etc at night' [ref:nfa-sleepy].
3. **By torchlight**: the Bloomfield method, a paperbark torch in the bow and a spear [ref:anderson1996].
4. **In a trap**: a [trap or fence](entry:fish-traps) across a narrow in the dry [ref:roth1901].
5. **Leave the guarding males** from October to February; the sheet of eggs under the log is next year's fish [ref:nfa-sleepy].
6. **Cook it** on the coals or in the [earth oven](entry:earth-oven); the flesh is white and flaky [ref:wiki-sleepy-cod].

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body:
- Crocodile water, especially at night by torchlight [ref:crocwise] [ref:kw-about].
- The sleepy cod is not listed in the Queensland freshwater size and possession table; the gear rules and the general rules apply [ref:qld-limits] [ref:qld-gear].
- Native title holders' fishing for personal, domestic or non-commercial communal needs is covered by section 211 of the *Native Title Act 1993* and section 14 of the *Fisheries Act 1994* [ref:alrc] [ref:qld-fishact].

sections.heading: On Country today
sections.body: Whether *kurrubal* is its name is for Kuku Yalanji speakers; the contribution box below is for that [ref:hershberger1982].

sections.heading: Language
sections.body: *[kurrubal](word:kurrubal)* 'fresh water cod'; *[kuyu](word:kuyu)* 'fish'; *[kurruba](word:kurruba)* 'species of freshwater fish'; *[wukuju](word:wukuju)* 'freshwater prawn, the big one with long legs'; *[yinba](word:yinba)* 'fish spear'; *[yirrmba](word:yirrmba)* 'many-pronged fish spear'; *[makarr](word:makarr)* 'fish net'; *[ngawurr-ngawun](word:ngawurr-ngawun)* 'freshwater crocodile' [ref:hershberger1982].

locations.summary: The sleepy cod lives in the Hann's waters. In a survey of anglers in Lakefield National Park (now Rinyirru), downstream of the Hann, in 1986–91, the freshwater catch included 'sleepy cod (Oxyeleotris lineolatus)' [ref:russell1993]. The Atlas of Living Australia holds only two records in a box of about 90 × 85 km around the middle Hann, Laura and western Rinyirru, both from 1972 [ref:ala-hann-fish]. The Hann never stops running, so its deep holes keep their water and their snags through the late dry [ref:bom-105001b].

sections.heading: Where it lives here
sections.body: The Hann is fed by springs: water 'seeps down through the high elevation sandstone and recharges the groundwater', and the larger springs 'supply base flow to several streams including … Jungle Creek and the Hann River in the west' [ref:wetlandinfo-normanby]. The gauge at Sandy Creek has not recorded a day without flow since 1968; flow is lowest from September to November [ref:bom-105001b]. So in the late dry the sleepy cod's water is a low run between deep holes, with snags and undercut banks for cover, not a cut-off pool.

sections.heading: How people fished here
sections.body:
No published record from this country names the sleepy cod. What is recorded is fishing in general:

- **Possum People (upper Hann)**: a Possum man described 'fishing for barra, jewfish, catties and spotties' [ref:fca-possum].
- **Thaypan**: 'We get wallaby, barramundi, freshwater fish and turtles and mussels' [ref:fca-thaypan].
- **Kuku Thaypan fish traps**: *Rungol* (hollow logs) 'that were cut from the Ku akulumbah Messmate woodland and used as fish traps', set in a lagoon [ref:standley2019]. Which fish they took is not recorded.
- **Kuku Warra (Laura)**: before fishing, 'I'll sing out to the old people and say "Hey old people, I'm coming to take some fish. I just want a little bit."', and after a good catch 'we must always leave three or four fish on the banks after we leave to show appreciation for the people of the country' [ref:fca-kukuwarra].

sections.heading: Safety here
sections.body: Estuarine crocodiles 'inhabit waterways and billabongs throughout Rinyirru' [ref:qpws-rinyirru-2013]. Night fishing at the water's edge is crocodile country; see [crocodiles](entry:crocodiles).

sections.heading: On country today
sections.body: The upper Hann is the Possum People's country and the middle and lower Hann are Thaypan country; their November 2023 determinations recognise rights to 'hunt, fish and gather on the land and waters of the area' [ref:fca-possum] [ref:fca-thaypan].

locations.summary: It is recorded within 30 km of [Karma Waters](place:karma-waters), and the dry-season pools with their snags and undercut banks are its country [ref:ala-karma-river].

sections.heading: What it eats here
sections.body: On the Mitchell, prawns 'featured prominently' in its diet [ref:jardine2012].

sections.heading: Where it lives here
sections.body: At Karma Waters the undercut banks, roots and snags of the dry-season pools are its places; the [waterhole](entry:waterhole) page describes the cover and the hot, low-oxygen water of the late dry that the sleepy cod's air-breathing helps it through [ref:waterhole-temps] [ref:fergusson-refuge].

sections.heading: Taking it here
sections.body: On the Mitchell, Palmer saw the freshwater mangrove *Barringtonia racemosa*, 'Yakoora', cut up, hammered fine and put in the lagoons, and the coolibah's branches and leaves 'laid in water for several days to sicken the fish; it is universally used for this purpose' [ref:palmer1883].

sections.heading: On country today
sections.body: The sleepy cod is in the Karma Waters pools and is the fish to teach children spearing on, because it lies still and is worth eating [ref:ala-karma-river] [ref:nfa-sleepy].
